NAVER D2SF-backed MOVIN Raises KRW 10 Billion Series A to Expand from Motion Capture to Motion Data Infrastructure
News provided by
NAVER D2SF
Nov 09, 2026, 11:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
MOVIN TRACIN reaches KRW 1 billion in global revenue within a year of launch, with expansion into robotics, live entertainment, sports and rehabilitation
MOVIN extends its technology from ultra-light devices to large-space, multi-person environments and plans to build a 330㎡ R&D center
SEOUL, South Korea , Nov. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- NAVER D2SF-backed MOVIN, a LiDAR-based 3D motion data AI company led by CEO Byeoli Choi, has raised KRW 10 billion in a Series A round. The round was led by IMM Investment, with participation from Industrial Bank of Korea (IBK) and Voyager Ventures. Existing investors Atinum Investment, NAVER D2SF, and Schmidt also made follow-on investments. This marks NAVER D2SF's third consecutive investment in MOVIN, following its seed investment in 2023 and the pre-Series A round in 2025. With the new funding, MOVIN plans to grow its motion capture business and build an R&D center of approximately 330 square meters to strengthen its technology development in physical AI.
Founded in 2023, MOVIN develops technology that converts human movement into precise 3D data. Its flagship solution, MOVIN TRACIN, combines LiDAR sensors and camera vision with the company's proprietary AI to capture movement in real time without suits or markers, replacing the complex setup and reducing the cost associated with conventional motion capture equipment. Building on this, MOVIN has secured global customers primarily in content production, including games, film, and virtual creators. Within a year of the product's commercial launch, overseas sales accounted for 70% of total revenue, reflecting growing demand in international markets.
Building on its core technology, MOVIN is developing industry-specific solutions to address evolving market needs. Global robotics companies and research institutes such as Boston Dynamics and the RAI Institute have used MOVIN's technology for robot teleoperation and training, and MOVIN TRACIN Lite, is being used by partners to collect human motion data for robot learning. MOVIN was also selected as the only South Korean Launching Adoption Partner for NVIDIA SOMA, integrating its technology to support robot learning with real-world human motion data. In live entertainment, MOVIN unveiled MOVIN TRACIN Stage, which tracks the movements of multiple performers simultaneously, at the 2026 NAB Show in the U.S. this April, where it also demonstrated integrations with Disguise and Notch. Based on these use cases, MOVIN plans to expand into live interactive content and shows, as well as sports, rehabilitation, and other industries that utilize human movement as data.
MOVIN, which raised a KRW 4 billion pre-Series A round last year, plans to use the new funding to advance its technology and grow its global business. Starting with MOVIN TRACIN, its single-person markerless motion capture solution, the company plans to extend its technology into on-device multimodal AI-based motion data infrastructure that supports everything from ultra-light devices to large-space, multi-person environments.
MOVIN is also expanding its R&D infrastructure. The planned R&D center will focus on collecting real-world multimodal datasets for world-model development and advancing MOVIN's AI and motion data processing technologies.

Five Australian startups that raised funding last week
From a $115 million raise for an AI “co-worker” platform to a $750,000 pre-seed for a trucking camera system, here’s who banked funding across the Australian startup scene last week.
Yajush Gupta
News · 8 Nov 2026 · 2 min read
☆ Save
Above Five Australian startups that raised funding last week . Dynamic Business
Five Australian startups closed funding rounds last week, ranging from a nine-figure raise that created the country’s newest tech unicorn down to early pre-seed cheques for logistics and national security tech. Here’s who raised what, who backed them, and what each company actually does.
Future Secure AI raised $115.3 million
Sydney-born startup Future Secure AI raised US$80 million (A$115.3 million) via convertible notes, in a round valuing the business at $1.7 billion and making it Australia’s newest tech unicorn, according to the Australian Financial Review. Square Peg, Yarra Capital Management and Firetrail led the round, alongside Macquarie Asset Management. It’s the company’s third funding round since it was founded three years ago, following a previous raise in June 2025.
Future Secure AI builds AI “co-workers” for large organisations, assembling teams of AI agents, each given a name and face, to handle complex tasks across investment banking, consulting, healthcare and law, overseen by a human supervisor. The company is reportedly targeting annual recurring revenue approaching $100 million by the end of 2026, and now operates out of Sydney, Melbourne, New York, Chicago, Austin, Toronto and São Paulo.
i14 raised $9 million
Melbourne AI infrastructure company i14 raised $9 million in a seed round from Salus Ventures, IP Group, Tin Alley Ventures, Hostplus, Archangel Ventures and Virescent Ventures, according to the Australian Financial Review.
i14 is developing technology that helps enterprises train large AI models while cutting compute energy use, an efficiency play aimed at reducing the escalating hardware and power costs that come with training frontier-scale models. The round lands amid a global chip and memory shortage, with i14 targeting neoclouds, hyperscalers and other heavy AI users looking to cut their compute bills.
Copy Geek raised $2 million
Sydney startup Copy Geek raised a $2 million pre-seed round for its non-custodial crypto trading platform, which lets professional traders automatically copy trades across partner exchanges. The round came from a group of angel investors, led by Dr David Issa and Thomas Boga. The funding will go toward product development, engineering, and signing further exchange partnerships.
Forward Deployed raised $1 million
Melbourne-based Forward Deployed raised $1 million from Innovation Victoria and Swinburne University of Technology to take its portable chemical threat detection platform into production. The company builds field-ready sensors designed to let defence and security teams identify hazards within seconds.
Indrus raised $750,000
Perth startup Indrus raised a $750,000 pre-seed round led by Purpose Ventures, with Melt Ventures and Curtin University also participating. Founders Ryan Liebregts and Dre Siwela met in a robotics class while studying mechatronics engineering at Curtin University. Indrus uses a site’s existing security cameras to automate yard and dock orchestration, helping logistics operators track trucks, trailers and equipment and cut truck turnaround times without installing new hardware.
